title: Boss: the supply-chain week
summary: A week of supply-chain work: a release gate that honours expiring risk acceptances, a lock-file diff that catches a package whose content changed under the same version, and log redaction for the keys that keep turning up in build output.

steps.title: The tickets
body: SEC-311  The release gate fails on every High advisory, even ones security has formally
accepted until a fix ships. Support accepted risks, but only until their expiry date.
SEC-312  A package's content changed while its version stayed 1.4.2 (a registry incident at a
mirror). Our lock file has contentHash for every package: diff lock files in CI.
SEC-313  Build logs contain API keys (verbose HTTP logging in integration tests). Redact them

steps.title: SEC-311: a gate with expiring acceptances
prompt: Write `List<string> Gate(List<Finding> findings, List<Accepted> accepted, DateOnly today)`. The records are given.
- only `High` and `Critical` findings can fail the gate;
- a finding is covered by an acceptance with the same `Advisory` **and** `Package` whose `Expires` is today or later;
- each uncovered High/Critical finding gives `"<Package> <Version> <Severity> <Advisory>"`, plus ` (acceptance expired <yyyy-MM-dd>)` when a matching acceptance exists but expired;
- Critical first, then by package (ordinal). An empty list means the release may ship.
starter: List<string> Gate(List<Finding> findings, List<Accepted> accepted, DateOnly today)
solution: List<string> Gate(List<Finding> findings, List<Accepted> accepted, DateOnly today)
var result = new List<(int Rank, string Package, string Line)>();
foreach (var f in findings.Where(f => f.Severity is "High" or "Critical"))
var matches = accepted.Where(a => a.Advisory == f.Advisory && a.Package == f.Package).ToList();
return result.OrderBy(r => r.Rank).ThenBy(r => r.Package, StringComparer.Ordinal).Select(r => r.Line).ToList();
template: new("GHSA-xxxx-0002", "Example.Compression", new DateOnly(2026, 12, 15), "not reachable: only used for test fixtures"),
new("GHSA-xxxx-0006", "Example.Pdf", new DateOnly(2026, 10, 31), "fix promised by vendor in October"),
Dojo.Eq("the gate on release day", new List<string>
Dojo.Eq("an acceptance is valid on its last day", new List<string>(), Gate(new List<Finding> { findings[0] }, accepted, new DateOnly(2026, 12, 15)));

Dojo.Eq("...and not the day after", new List<string> { "Example.Compression 1.4.2 High GHSA-xxxx-0002 (acceptance expired 2026-12-15)" }, Gate(new List<Finding> { findings[0] }, accepted, new DateOnly(2026, 12, 16)));
Dojo.Eq("no findings, no failures", new List<string>(), Gate(new List<Finding>(), accepted, today));
record Finding(string Package, string Version, string Severity, string Advisory);
record Accepted(string Advisory, string Package, DateOnly Expires, string Reason);
hints: For each High/Critical finding, find the acceptances with the same advisory and package. Any with `Expires >= today` covers it.
Collect `(rank, package, line)` and sort with `OrderBy(rank).ThenBy(package, StringComparer.Ordinal)`. Format a `DateOnly` with `:yyyy-MM-dd`.

steps.title: SEC-312: diff two lock files
prompt: Write `List<string> LockDiff(string before, string after)` (`using System.Text.Json;`). Both are `packages.lock.json` files:
Compare package by package (a package is identified by framework and id). Output, sorted with ordinal order:
- `+ <framework> <id> <resolved>` for a new package, `- <framework> <id> <resolved>` for a removed one;
- `! <framework> <id> <resolved> content changed` when the version is the **same** but `contentHash` differs: the one that must stop the build.

hints: Read each file into a dictionary keyed by `(framework, id)` with `(resolved, contentHash)`: `GetProperty("dependencies").EnumerateObject()`, then `EnumerateObject()` again for the packages.
Walk the new file for `+`, `~` and `!`, the old one for `-`, then `Sort(StringComparer.Ordinal)` (`!` < `+` < `-` < `~` in ordinal order).

steps.title: SEC-313: redact keys in build logs
prompt: Write `string Redact(string line)` (`using System.Text.RegularExpressions;`). Each value that the scanner rule from the secrets lesson finds (keyword, `:` or `=`, 12+ characters from `A-Za-z0-9_-.+/=`) is replaced by its **first 4 characters** followed by `****`. Everything else in the line stays exactly as it was. Here every such value is redacted, whatever its entropy: a log is not the place to be clever.
Authorization header token=dt_7Hq2Lw9xPz4Rk8Vb sent   ->  Authorization header token=dt_7**** sent
template: Dojo.Eq("a token in a log line", "Authorization header token=dt_7**** sent", Redact("Authorization header token=dt_7Hq2Lw9xPz4Rk8Vb sent"));
Dojo.Eq("two secrets on one line", "password=hunt**** secret: Zq8L****", Redact("password=hunter2hunter2 secret: Zq8Lw2Pn5Rt9Vx3K"));
Dojo.Eq("short values are left alone", "password=hunter2", Redact("password=hunter2"));
Dojo.Eq("lines without secrets are unchanged", "GET /api/products 200 12ms", Redact("GET /api/products 200 12ms"));
hints: `Regex.Replace(line, pattern, m => ...)` with two groups: everything up to the value, and the value.
